answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may vote on trades or claim rewards. The protocol caps each identity’s influence by its bonded stake, then slashes the bond when a challenge proves coordinated self-dealing under predefined rules. Splitting stake across fake accounts therefore adds no influence, while each account incurs fees and capital locked beyond its planning horizon. The ferrous token’s price delta also exposes the attacker to market risk.
